label: The Dante Leaf
language: Italian vernacular in Latin alphabet, in a late-medieval Gothic/humanistic book hand with red rubrics
summary: The plate shows a two-column Italian vernacular verse text on an illuminated leaf, with a red rubric in the right column announcing the beginning of the first chapter of the third comedy of Paradise by Dante Alighieri (spelled alleghien), in which Beatrice shows the narrator the glory of Paradise leading him from heaven to heaven; the left column ends with a line about being disposed to rise to the stars, and the page is framed by a richly coloured floral border with birds and a central miniature of a robed female figure.

Left column lines 3-4 and 7-13: several words are blurred by small scale and red initials, so readings such as 'se[?]onte' and 'Quato [?]he' are tentative.
Left line 46 'P[?]uo [?] disposto ad salire alle stelle' - words after the initial are only partly legible, though 'disposto ad salire alle stelle' is comparatively clear.
Right top 'Ne la cl[?] che piu de' - the word after 'la' is abbreviated/illegible.
Right main lines 1-6 and 16-29: many syllables in the lower right column are faint, e.g. 'Percha pre[?]' and 'celphis[?]ca', and are hedged.
The small '54' at top right of the printed page: uncertain whether printed plate/folio number or handwritten annotation, due to its size.
Miniature figure attributes are painted but small; identification beyond a robed female figure is not assumed from the image alone.
verdictSummary: The search found standard editions, summaries and a similarly worded catalog description that identify the main text as the opening of Dante's Paradiso, Canto I, and match its opening verses in general terms, but no published transcription or catalog record of plate 54 of this specific illuminated leaf, with its manuscript rubric, layout, border and miniature, was presented to check against the blind transcription.
